body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Tuesday, August 18, 2026, and we’re waking up to a warm one — expect a high near 98° today under clear skies. Overnight, a truck fire that spread into hillside vegetation west of town drew a heavy response, and a 53-foot trailer went fully involved north of Pond. We’ll have the details on that, plus the latest on the arrest in Monday’s deadly South Bakersfield stabbing, all in today’s brief.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most significant incident unfolded around 9:47 p.m. when a truck fire that reportedly tipped over and burned down a trailer pushed into the hillside west of Bakersfield and escalated into a wildland response. Multiple engines, a dozer, helicopter 409, and a water tender were among the ordered resources. Crews worked to access the burn, with the reporting party pointing out lights on the hill as firefighters battled the blaze.

Just before 3:45 a.m., a 53-foot trailer north of Pond on Garzoli Road was fully involved, with a spot of grass fire spreading alongside it. Battalion crews responded to what dispatch dubbed the Garzoli Incident and remained on scene for hotspots.

In the south end, just before 10:45 p.m., a caller reported roughly 30 shots fired, mostly in a field in the area of Panama Lane and South Allen Road. The call stood for service while units investigated.

Around 3:06 a.m., a welfare check near the Wells Fargo on Columbus Street escalated — a man on a bicycle was approached by subjects and an impact sound was heard, followed by a fight involving three people. Two suspects fled northbound Columbus; units searched.

Just after 4 a.m., a big-rig incident with a load of table grapes brought a roadway closure in Delano, with Environmental Health notified.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 98° and a low around 73° tonight. It’s currently 91° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County. Air quality is holding at 77 — moderate — and no active fires are currently reported in the county.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that a 21-year-old woman is in custody after a man was allegedly stabbed and killed at a South Bakersfield home Monday afternoon.** Officers responded to a home in the 400 block of White Lane around 3:30 p.m., where they found a man who had been stabbed. He was pronounced dead at the scene. Homicide detectives investigated and arrested Erionna Russel, 21, on suspicion of second-degree murder. Police say Russel and the victim knew each other. Russel is scheduled to appear in court Wednesday afternoon. The victim’s identity has not yet been released.

**KGET 17 tells us that a California City man was arrested after hundreds of pounds of narcotics and a firearm were seized.** Details on the arrest and the investigation are still emerging, but the seizure marks a significant haul in the ongoing effort to combat drug trafficking in the region.

**According to 23ABC, new CDC data shows kindergarten vaccination rates are slipping across the country, raising questions about how many children are starting school without all of their required shots.** National vaccination coverage among kindergarteners fell by 0.1% for all reported vaccines during the 2025-26 school year. At the same time, exemptions from one or more vaccines rose to 4.2%, up from 3.6% the year before. The CDC says about 280,000 kindergarteners nationwide went into the 2025-26 school year without documentation of completing the MMR series. The report follows Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s visit to Kern County, where he described vaccine hesitancy as part of a broader crisis of public trust. "If the public does not trust the public health agencies, we are not going to have public health," Kennedy said. The latest CDC data show California's kindergarten MMR rate at 95.7%. According to the state's 2024-25 data, Kern County's overall immunization rate was 85.4%, which included virtual schools. When looking at classroom-based schools, that rate rises to 93.7%, similar to the state average. Kern Public Health says virtual schools may be exempt from immunization requirements. California law requires children entering TK through 12th grade to have documentation of required vaccinations. Unlike many states, California does not allow religious or personal-belief exemptions. Some students can still be admitted conditionally while they complete their vaccine series. Schools are required to follow up with families, and if a child does not come into compliance, they may be excluded from school.

**KGET 17 shares that the fight to save the Crystal Palace in Bakersfield continues as one offer on the table would mean tearing it down.** Buck Owens opened the Crystal Palace in 1996, creating a home for the Bakersfield Sound. Country singer Scotty Crabtree, who started visiting the Palace in 1999 and says performing with its house band years later helped launch his career, has started an online petition that has now gathered more than 200 signatures. The Buck Owens Private Foundation confirms it has received several offers — including one still on the table that would tear the building down. In a written statement, foundation representative Jim Shaw said the hope is to find a buyer who will reopen and reimagine the venue. "Since the listing and closing of the Crystal Palace last year we've had quite a bit of interest and several offers (including one still on the table that would be a tear-down!!). Our hope is that sooner rather than later the right person will step forward with a plan to reopen the venue in a manner that will bring our beautiful building back to life. Although in our perfect world the theme would remain Buck and the Bakersfield Sound, we accept that the new iteration might not resemble the version that we all remember. There are numerous ways that the venue could be reimagined," Shaw said.

## Something good

Bakersfield residents are pushing for more trees and cleaner air as heat and pollution concerns grow. This community effort aims to improve local environmental conditions, and it’s a reminder that even small steps can make a big difference in our quality of life here in Kern County.

## Coming up this week

The Multi Modal Transportation And Traffic Safety Committee meets today, August 18, at 12:00 p.m. The Historic Preservation Commission convenes later today at 4:00 p.m. On August 19, the Water Board meets at 10:00 a.m. The Planning Commission gathers on August 20 at 5:30 p.m. And the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission meets today at 2:00 p.m.

On the events front, Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio take the stage at the Fox Theater on August 22. The Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027 begins at the Fox Theater on August 24. Rodney Carrington performs at the Fox Theater on August 27. CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE hits the Fox Theater on August 28. Willie Barcena takes the stage at the Fox Theater on August 29, and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix performs at the Fox Theater on August 29 as well.
